title: Day 971: Netanyahu Condemns Haredi Attack on Supreme Court Justice; Supreme Court President Amit Calls Riot 'A Pogrom' and 'Attack on Rule of Law' — 62 Arrested
detail: On June 4, 2026 (Day 971 / Ceasefire Day 238), the political and judicial fallout from the Haredi extremist attack on Supreme Court Deputy President Noam Sohlberg's home dominated Israeli public discourse. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu issued his 'strongest condemnation' of the attack after calling Sohlberg personally, declaring the violence 'completely unacceptable' and vowing accountability for those arrested. Netanyahu's condemnation placed him in an unusual position: he was distancing himself from violence carried out by supporters of ultra-Orthodox parties whose Knesset votes keep his coalition in power, and whose conscription-exemption demands he has repeatedly backed. Supreme Court President Isaac Amit stated the Haredi assault on Sohlberg's home 'crossed a red line,' called it 'a pogrom,' and characterized it as 'an attack on the rule of law and the foundations of democracy.' 62 suspects were arrested by Israeli police in connection with the attack. Israeli opposition leaders pointed to the attack as emblematic of the deepening institutional crisis facing Israel: the same Supreme Court targeted by the mob is scheduled to rule by July 1, 2026 — 27 days away — on whether the Netanyahu government has established a credible October 7 accountability framework. The convergence of violence against the judiciary and the looming accountability ruling created what Haaretz described as an 'unprecedented constitutional moment' for Israeli democracy. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara opened an investigation. Israel's Police Commissioner vowed additional charges for the protesters arrested in connection with the Sohlberg attack.

media.caption: Supreme Court President Amit: Haredi rampage at Justice Sohlberg's home was 'a pogrom' and 'an attack on the rule of law' — Netanyahu issues strongest condemnation; 62 arrested

title: Day 971: Haredi Draft Crisis Converges With October 7 Accountability Countdown — Attack on Judiciary Erupts 27 Days Before Supreme Court July 1 Ruling
detail: On June 4, 2026 (Day 971 / Ceasefire Day 238), Israeli analysts noted the unprecedented collision of two institutional crises: the Haredi draft conscription confrontation — which escalated into extremist violence against a Supreme Court justice's home — converging with the October 7 accountability countdown that culminates in a Supreme Court ruling in 27 days. The Haredi rioters who attacked Deputy President Sohlberg's home on June 3 were protesting the Supreme Court's April 2026 ruling that Haredi draft exemptions were constitutionally impermissible without formal legislation. The same Supreme Court — the same institution the rioters attacked — is scheduled to rule by July 1 on whether the Netanyahu government's Kallner inquiry bill satisfies minimum October 7 accountability requirements. Legal scholars cited by Haaretz and the Jerusalem Post noted that the mob attack on a sitting justice cannot be divorced from Netanyahu's coalition's broader war on judicial authority: the government has for over two years blocked an independent October 7 probe, pushed legislation stripping judicial review powers, and sustained coalition partners who have repeatedly undermined the court's legitimacy. The Israeli opposition, October Council (bereaved families forum), and legal experts framed the June 3–4 Sohlberg attack as the logical endpoint of years of institutional delegitimization — a democratic erosion that intersects directly with the refusal to establish an independent October 7 investigation. Accountability advocates noted that the Beyachad alliance (Bennett-Lapid) had explicitly pledged to restore both judicial independence and a full October 7 commission as Day 1 priorities. No new Hamas Al-Qassam Brigades supreme commander has been named on Day 971. Imad Aqel remains the NILI task force's last primary target.

media.caption: 62 Haredim arrested after violent attack on Supreme Court justice's home — Haredi draft crisis converges with October 7 accountability countdown 27 days before July 1 Supreme Court ruling
